deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a Latin draft of the opening of Riemann's 1861 essay for the Paris Academy prize (published posthumously as the 'Commentatio mathematica, qua respondere tentatur quaestioni ab Ill.ma Academia Parisiensi propositae', Werke 1876). The page sets up the problem and the change-of-variables formalism; the previous page is a cleaner copy of its lower half.

(0) Programme. The Academy's question will be treated by first solving a more general one: what must the conductivity properties of the body and the heat distribution be for there to exist a system of lines that remain isothermal for all time? From the general solution one then selects the cases where the properties are everywhere the same, i.e. the body is homogeneous. Only bodies are considered in which the conductivity is the same in opposite directions, which gives a symmetric conductivity tensor.

(1) Equation I. Let u(t,x) be the temperature at the point (x1,x2,x3) at time t. Then
  sum_i d/dx_i ( sum_j a_ij du/dx_j ) = h du/dt.
Here:
- a_ij = a_ji are the 'resultant conductivities', given functions of x;
- h is the specific heat per unit volume, i.e. specific heat times density;
- the quadratic form (a_ij) is positive definite.

(2) Variational form (A). For an admissible u the expression
  delta ∫∫∫ sum a_ij u_{x_i} u_{x_j} dx + ∫∫∫ 2h u_t delta u dx
depends only on the value of the variation delta u on the boundary surface. [My filling:] Integrating by parts, the first variation is 2∫ sum a_ij u_{x_j} delta u_{x_i} = boundary term − 2∫ div(a grad u) delta u. Its vanishing for interior variations, with u_t held fixed, is exactly equation I.

(3) Change of variables (B). Introduce new independent variables s1,s2,s3 in place of the rectangular coordinates. The functional becomes
  delta ∫ sum b_mn u_{s_m} u_{s_n} ds + ∫ 2k u_t delta u ds,
with
  b_mn = (1/J) sum_ij a_ij (ds_m/dx_i)(ds_n/dx_j),  k = h/J,  J = det(ds/dx).
[My filling:] u_{x_i} = sum_m P_mi u_{s_m} with P = ds/dx, and dx = ds/J. In matrix form b = P a P^T / J.

(4) Determinants and adjugate forms. Let A = det(a), B = det(b), and let alpha_ij and beta_ij be the cofactors (forma adjuncta), so alpha = A a^{-1} and beta = B b^{-1}. Riemann states:
- A = B J;
- beta_mn = sum_ij alpha_ij (dx_i/ds_m)(dx_j/ds_n);
- hence sum alpha_ij dx_i dx_j = sum beta_mn ds_m ds_n, i.e. the adjugate form is a covariant quadratic differential form (a metric);
- also h/A = k/B (stated on the previous page).
[My verification:]
- B = J^{-3} (det P)^2 A = A/J.
- b^{-1} = J P^{-T} a^{-1} P^{-1}, so beta = B b^{-1} = (A/J) J P^{-T} a^{-1} P^{-1} = P^{-T} alpha P^{-1}, with P^{-1} = dx/ds.
- k/B = (h/J)/(A/J) = h/A.

Purpose (stated on the next page): the transformation of equation I is thereby reduced to the transformation of the quadratic differential form sum alpha_ij dx_i dx_j. The question whether u can depend on t and only two of the s-variables becomes a question of when a form sum b ds ds can be brought into a given form sum alpha dx dx. Riemann says this is to be handled by Gauss's method from surface theory; this leads to his curvature conditions in the published Commentatio.
errors: No mathematical errors. The relations A = B J, beta = P^{-T} alpha P^{-1}, b = P a P^T / J and k = h/J are all correct (J taken as the positive Jacobian det(ds/dx)).

Equation I is written only with its first term, the remaining terms being indicated by '+'. The functional (A)/(B) is written without '= 0' or an explicit statement of what is held fixed; one must understand u_t as not varied and the identity as holding modulo boundary terms.

In the 2x3 array notation for the symmetric forms, the off-diagonal entries are inconsistently labelled (e.g. b_{2,3}, b_{1,2}, b_{3,1} versus beta_{1,2}, beta_{2,1}, ...). This is a notational slip in a draft.

results.what: Anisotropic inhomogeneous heat equation div(a grad u) = h u_t with symmetric positive definite conductivity tensor
Variational (Dirichlet-type) formulation of the heat equation with u_t fixed
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Dirichlet, Thomson; Riemann's use of the Dirichlet principle

results.what: Transformation law of the conductivity tensor and specific heat under change of coordinates: b = P a P^T/J, k = h/J
results.modern_name: Tensor density transformation of a contravariant (2,0) tensor (Laplace-Beltrami structure)

results.what: The adjugate of the conductivity form, sum alpha_ij dx_i dx_j, transforms as a quadratic differential form (metric), with A = BJ and h/A = k/B invariant
results.modern_name: Conductivity tensor defines a Riemannian metric g = adj(a); reduction of the PDE problem to the equivalence problem for metrics

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the opening of Riemann's well-known 1861 Paris prize essay (Commentatio mathematica, Werke 1876). The reduction of heat conduction to the transformation of the quadratic form sum alpha dx dx is exactly the published approach. Only draft-level variations are new.

checkable.sympy: P=Matrix(3,3,symbols('p0:9')); a=Matrix(3,3,lambda i,j: Symbol('a%d%d'%(min(i,j),max(i,j)))); J=P.det(); b=P*a*P.T/J; simplify(a.det()-b.det()*J)==0
checkable.asserts: A = B * J, where b = P a P^T / J and J = det(ds/dx)

checkable.asserts: beta_{mu,nu} = sum alpha_{i,j} dx_i/ds_mu dx_j/ds_nu (adjugate transforms covariantly)

transcription_corrections: Line after 'invenitur': the image shows a crossed-out left-hand side (roughly 'A dx1 dx2 / dx1'). The intended equation is A = B Σ± ∂s1/∂x1 ∂s2/∂x2 ∂s3/∂x3, as in the clean copy on the previous page.
First line: the interlinear insertion above 'prius' reads approximately 'eam qua' (or 'cum qua'); it is uncertain.
In 'Forma (a11 a22 a33 / a12) est forma positiva' the second row of the array is incompletely written in the manuscript, not omitted by the transcriber.

The word read as 'conductibilitas' in the inserted phrase about opposite directions likely reads 'conductibilitas eadem binis [directionibus]'. The sense is that conductivity is the same in opposite directions, i.e. a_ij = a_ji.
